feed.title: NPR Topics: Home Page Top Stories
feed.subtitle: Top stories in the U.S. and world news, politics, health, science, business, music, arts and culture. Nonprofit journalism with a mission. This is NPR.

entry.title: U.S. to issue visas to Flávio Bolsonaro as his whereabouts remain unclear
entry.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro leaves Brazil for the U.S. amid a money-laundering probe, as Washington agrees to issue visas to him and his family.

entry.title: Southwest flood damage estimates are hundreds of millions for New Mexico alone
entry.summary: Intense rainstorms linked to a very active El Niño-driven Pacific hurricane season have left thousands of people in the Four Corners states displaced.

entry.title: Israel's voter turnout soars as Netanyahu faces a tight election
entry.summary: Israelis voted in their highest numbers in over two decades in a tense national election to decide whether to stick with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's far-right coalition.

entry.title: Romantasy fans turn out for 'Midnight Maas' release event
entry.summary: The highly anticipated, latest installment of Sarah J. Maas' romantasy series has hit the shelves. Hardcore fans were lined up (in their faerie ears) at the stroke of midnight.

entry.title: A judge halted D.C. golf course renovations. Trump says they'll still start next month
entry.summary: A federal judge has barred the government from clearing more trees or making other alterations to D.C.'s East Potomac Park without proper notice. Trump says his administration will appeal.

entry.title: Filmmaking is 'our weapon against intolerance,' say 'La Bola Negra' directors
entry.summary: Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi have turned four pages of an unfinished play by Federico García Lorca into a sweeping epic that spans 90 years of Spanish history, focusing on the stories of gay men.

entry.title: Bolsonaro's party accepts Brazil election defeat, but he refuses to concede
entry.summary: Brazil's opposition party accepts President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's election victory, but Flávio Bolsonaro won't concede, while President Trump calls the vote "rigged" without offering evidence.

entry.title: Discursive Verses: Jay-Z, the Super Bowl and playing with house money
entry.summary: NPR Music culture critic and reporter Rodney Carmichael ruminates on the latest in rap culture. This week: Is the rap mogul's self-selection a crowning achievement or a final affront?

entry.title: A 'Green Army' is out to thwart El Niño flooding
entry.summary: In Nairobi, a city prone to floods, workers in the "Green Army" are making preparations to prevent disaster when El Niño arrives.
